land.text: the enclave round Kammata Durga near Ballari that Singeya Nayaka III held as a Hoysala commander

predecessors.note: 'The founder was a Hoysala commander, Singeya Nayaka-III'; Cliopatria's Hoysala shapes of 1285-1326 do not contain the enclave (0 of 23 cells), so Cliopatria draws it as nobody's or Kampili's from 1285.

land.text: 'The Kampili kingdom then fell to the invasion in 1327 CE from the north' to Muhammad bin Tughluq's forces

successors.note: Cliopatria runs the row to 1332 and its Tughlaq shape takes the enclave only in 1333.

land.text: 'The Vijayanagara Empire emerged in 1336 CE from the remains of this kingdom'

successors.note: Not at the end: the empire arises nine years after the Tughlaq conquest, on the same land.

capitals.name: Kammata Durga (near Ballari)
capitals.note: The page names Kammata Durga as the only capital and says the kingdom 'existed near Ballari' on the Tungabhadra; the coordinates are Ballari's (gazetteer), not the fort's.

rulers.name: Singeya Nayaka III
rulers.note: The page gives '1280-1300'; the dossier starts in 1285 with Cliopatria.

rulers.name: Kampilideva
rulers.note: 'Nayaka-III was succeeded by his son Kampilideva in 1300 CE'; 'the last Kampili king', with inscriptions dated 1309 and 1326, who died in the fall of 1327.

keyframe_review.note: 5,373 km2 (21 cells) near Ballari on the Tungabhadra, as the page places the kingdom ('existed near Ballari'); the page gives no area. The outline stands for 1285-1325. The page has Singeya Nayaka III, 'a Hoysala commander', declaring independence in 1294, so 1285-1293 is a Hoysala commander's march and not an independent state (a subordination the Hoysala dossier, as suzerain, would record; the ledger convention puts vassal events on the suzerain), but the land is Kampili's in either reading, so the shape is kept from 1285.

The shape stands for 1326-1327 and ends there: 'The Kampili kingdom then fell to the invasion in 1327 CE from the north' and the page speaks of the kingdom's destruction after a defeat and a jauhar in 1327. Cliopatria keeps the row to 1332 (5,836 km2) and adds the 23 cells to the Tughlaq shape only in 1333 (14 of them); the Tughlaq dossier's tughlaq-dynasty_1327 keyframe takes the enclave from 1327.

correction.text: the Cliopatria 1326 outline, for 1326-1327 only; from 1327 it is Tughlaq land

region.text: the enclave round Kammata Durga near Ballari

ledger.note: 1285: Kampili appears at Kammata Durga on the Tungabhadra. Page silent on 1285 (Cliopatria's first year): Singeya Nayaka III is given as reigning 1280-1300 and as a Hoysala commander who 'declared independence' in 1294 (the page does not say how he held the land before), so 1285-1293 is a march under the Hoysalas; the kingdom 'existed near Ballari'.

region.text: the Kampili enclave, passing to the Tughlaq dynasty

ledger.note: 1327: Kampili falls to Muhammad bin Tughluq. 'The Kampili kingdom then fell to the invasion in 1327 CE from the north'; Malik Zada's army sent news of victory by delivering 'the straw-stuffed beheaded head and body of the dead Hindu king Kampilideva', and the page records a jauhar. The Tughlaq dynasty page lists 'Kampila' among the lands Muhammad attacked and plundered.

wars.name: Tughlaq conquest of Kampili
wars.outcome: Kampili destroyed; Kampilideva killed and his head sent to Delhi; the land becomes Tughlaq territory.
wars.note: The page gives no month and no battle name; Malik Zada commanded the army.

certainty.note: A district of about 5,000 km2 round one fort; the page gives no boundary.

notes: Kampili Kingdom: two Cliopatria shapes (1285-1332) reviewed against one page (Kampili Kingdom, whose infobox is not in the text the fetch returned: no area, no founding or ending date other than those quoted in the ledger) and, for the 1327 context, the Tughlaq dynasty page. Page budget 1-2, so no second page. Dates: start 1285 is Cliopatria's (the page gives the founder's reign as 1280-1300 and his independence in 1294, which ends his status as a Hoysala commander; no vassal event is written because the suzerain records those); end 1327 is the page's, Cliopatria's 1332 is five years late. The Hoysala dossier of sa-03 has the Hoysala page's line 'By 1336, the Sultan had conquered ... the tiny Kingdom of Kampili', which agrees with 1327 as the fall and 1336 as the settlement. The page's claim that Delhi forces were killed by the Yadavas in 1294 does not match the Khalji pages (Devagiri raid 1296, Kafur 1307-08); it is quoted, not corrected. Vijayanagara: the page says the empire emerged in 1336 from the remains of this kingdom; the Vijayanagara dossier belongs to another part of sa-04. Region names: none missing (the enclave is drawn from the Cliopatria shape).
